title: Education Services for Overseas Students Amendment (Cost Recovery and Other Measures) Bill 2021
short_title: Education Services for Overseas Students Amendment (Cost Recovery and Other Measures) Bill 2021

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would update how the government recovers costs from education providers that enrol overseas students.

It would do this by clarifying that compliance audits are an explicit power of the agencies that regulate registered providers, and by setting the annual registration charge due date at 30 days after the department issues an invoice.
The explanatory memorandum says the bill is one of four separate bills that together implement a new cost recovery model announced in the 2021–22 Budget.
changes: Makes explicit that ESOS agencies can conduct compliance audits of the providers they regulate.
Sets the due date for a provider's CRICOS annual registration charge to 30 days after the Secretary invoices them.
Aligns the invoicing period under the ESOS Act with the payment rules under the TPS Levies Act.
summary.affected: Registered providers of courses for overseas students and the ESOS agencies that regulate them.

speeches.speaker: Alan Tudge
speeches.brief: The Education Services for Overseas Students Amendment (Cost Recovery and Other Measures) Bill 2021 was moved to amend the ESOS Act 2000, requiring registered providers to be in good standing with all ESOS agencies, clarifying compliance audit powers, and making the CRICOS annual registration charge payable within 30 days, with the new charging arrangements commencing on 1 January 2022.

speeches.speaker: Graham Perrett
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the bills as they reduce charges on international education providers by $7 million a year, but criticised the Morrison government for damaging higher education, jeopardising jobs and research, and using ministerial discretion to avoid parliamentary scrutiny.
